transcript:
Header: 2026-05-11 14:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Olivia Park (Redwood AE); Diego Morales (Redwood SE); Maya Chen (Redwood SE); Priya Rao (AuroraCloud PM); Liam O'Connor (AuroraCloud Integrations); Sofia Mendes (AuroraCloud Security)

Summary: Quick technical sync to align on reference architecture for the joint solution, clarify marketplace listing artifacts, and surface security/compliance requirements. Agreed next steps: SE to produce arch diagram, AE to iterate marketplace draft, customer to share SOC2 scope.

Topics: marketplace listing fields, reference architecture (VPC, private deployment, auth), joint solution integrations (billing, telemetry), security artifacts (SOC2, KMS, RBAC), go-to-market cadence.

Transcript:
[00:00] Olivia (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining.. we'll try to keep this to about 45 minutes. quick intro round?
[00:18] Priya (AuroraCloud): hi I'm Priya, partner PM on the Aurora marketplace program, thanks for scheduling.
[00:27] Liam (AuroraCloud): Liam here, I own cloud integrations, mostly the onboarding/ops side.
[00:33] Sofia (AuroraCloud): Sofia, security architect, I'll be asking a lot of questions about data flows.
[00:39] Diego (Redwood SE): Diego here, I'll drive the tech parts—reference arch, deployment patterns, things like KV cache and VPC peering.
[00:47] Olivia: cool, agenda — arch diagram, listing metadata, compliance, next steps.
[01:14] Priya: for context, AuroraCloud wants a joint listing in our marketplace with a reference architecture and a joint solution tile. we need to understand what's required from Redwood and what artifacts we can show in the listing.
[01:40] Olivia: got it. typical asks are: short product blurb, supported deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private), icons/screenshots, architecture diagram, security/compliance bullets, and a pricing range.
[02:05] Liam: on the ops side we need clear runtime requirements — GPU class, networking, any special kernel/compilation needs so our onboarding can size instances.
[02:27] Diego: yep, from Redwood's side we can provide recommended instance types per model family, expected token throughput, and notes on quantization/optimizations. small caveat — some of our internal kernel names might be mis-typed in docs sometimes (eg. "Redwood Dedicatedy" in older slides), we'll clean that up.
[02:48] Sofia: where does customer data flow? if it's a private deployment in their VPC, do logs leave the VPC? is KV cache persisted? we need clear statements for compliance.
[03:12] Maya (Redwood): good Q—private deployments keep all inference traffic inside the customer's VPC; we have optional audit log forwarding, but default logs are retained per agreement and can be disabled. KV cache is ephemeral in the runtime by default but can be configured to persist to a customer-managed store if they opt in.
[03:40] Priya: can you put that in writing? Aurora's listing requires a short security bullet and a link to a more detailed doc.
[03:52] Diego: yes we'll add a 2-3 line security summary and a link to our Partner Security pack.
[04:07] Olivia: we'll attach the partner security pack and SOC2 pointer to the marketplace assets. speaking of SOC2, Sofia, what exact scope do you need?
[04:24] Sofia: we need the SOC2 report and the list of in-scope controls; also encryption-at-rest / KMS usage, RBAC, SSO (SAML/OIDC) support, and audit log retention options.
[04:41] Diego: Redwood supports KMS integration, HSM via customer-managed keys for private deployments, and SAML SSO for console access. We can document key rotation expectations.
[04:58] Priya: great. on the reference architecture: Aurora wants a diagram that shows network flow - marketplace -> provisioning -> VPC -> instances. can you produce a diagram showing both hosted and private variants?
[05:22] Diego: yes we'll do two variants: hosted API integration (no customer VPC) and private/VPC deployment with peering and optional on-prem. we'll call out how smart routing and fallbacks work (latency/cost policies).
[05:48] Olivia: we should also include a short note on billing integration — marketplace billing vs direct Redwood billing for dedicated reservations. Liam, what's Aurora's preferred flow?
[06:05] Liam: we support both. preferred is marketplace-managed billing for simpler buyer experience, but for enterprise contracts we can support direct billing references. we need the metadata field 'billingOptions' populated in the listing.
[06:26] Olivia: ok we'll provide a matrix of billing options and which features are supported under each.
[06:39] [06:39] (minor crosstalk)
[07:02] Diego: technical deep-dive: models and kernel needs — if you plan to list Redwood-verified models, we will include recommended config (batch sizes, quantization profile). some older models require a different kernel path; we'll flag compatibility.
[07:30] Priya: can you give a simple performance number for each model class? even ballpark QPS / p99 latency helps us size nodes.
[07:45] Diego: yes. example: 8x A100-class can do ~3200 tokens/s for medium prompts under our continuous batching profile; p99 depends on batching policy but we can provide sample graphs. note these are approximate—workloads vary.
[08:12] Sofia: latency vs cost tradeoffs are important for our customers. do you support graceful degradation / fallbacks to smaller models?
[08:28] Maya: yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants or lower-cost quantized versions when capacity is constrained. we'll document which endpoints support automatic fallbacks.
[08:50] Priya: on the marketplace UI, we want two CTA buttons: "Deploy (Host in Aurora)" and "Contact Sales" for enterprise. does Redwood have an API for provisioning so we can wire the deploy flow?
[09:10] Diego: we expose a provisioning API for Dedicated/Private provisioning; we also have a cloud-init style payload for on-prem. we can provide sample API calls.
[09:27] Olivia: we'll put a sample 'deploy' payload in the listing assets repo.
[09:40] Liam: security checklist again—do you have a short doc with network ports, inbound/outbound rules, and logging endpoints?
[09:51] Diego: yes, I'll attach our network requirements doc. small transcription note: our doc sometimes references "KV cache" as "K-V cash" in older transcriptions so ignore those typos.
[10:08] Priya: thanks. about the marketing collateral — Aurora wants a short joint-solution blurb and 2-3 screenshots or a short gif. can Redwood provide those?
[10:21] Olivia: yes, we can provide a 2-paragraph blurb and up to three screenshots. we'll host assets on a shared drive link.
[10:30] Priya: excellent. one more operational Q — healthchecks and tracing hooks for Redwood runtime, can we surface them in Aurora's monitoring?
[10:41] Maya: yes we support metrics export (Prometheus), tracing spans, and per-route logs via our observability API. we can provide sample dashboards for your marketplace customers.
[11:00] Liam: good. next, on legal/compliance: are there any export controls or restricted models we should flag in the listing?
[11:12] Diego: at present we maintain a list of restricted models for export control; we'll add a column in the asset manifest to flag restricted content.
[11:25] Sofia: also need to confirm data residency options — can Redwood pin inference to certain regions so logs and outputs stay in-region?
[11:39] Diego: yes region pinning is supported for both hosted and dedicated modes; private deployments of course run in customer's region. we'll include region availability in the listing.
[11:53] Priya: timeline — Aurora wants listings live in 3 weeks if possible, is that realistic?
[12:03] Olivia: 3 weeks is aggressive but doable if we get security artifacts and the arch diagram this week. otherwise 4-5 weeks is safer.
[12:15] Priya: we'll try to get SOC2 pointer by EOD Friday.
[12:22] Sofia: I'll check which artifacts we can share publicly and what needs an NDA.
[12:30] Olivia: noted, we'll prepare a minimal public security summary and keep detailed reports behind the partner portal link.
[12:44] Diego: technical note — when you list vetted models, call out quantization profiles; e.g., 4-bit quantized models have different latency and memory needs.
[12:58] Liam: got it. for the marketplace manifest, what fields are required? name, short/long description, pricing, screenshots, architecture diagram, security bullets, billingOptions, regionAvailability, provisioning API endpoint?
[13:15] Olivia: yes that's basically it. we'll send a sample manifest.
[13:32] Priya: can you also provide a sample SSO flow for the Aurora console linking with Redwood tenant for joint customers?
[13:45] Maya: yes, SAML flow sample and metadata XML — we'll provide that.
[13:56] [13:56] (brief silence)
[14:10] Olivia: let's recap next steps — Diego to produce arch diagrams, Olivia to iterate marketplace draft and pricing ranges, Sofia to confirm security artifacts, Priya to confirm marketplace SLA.
[14:33] Priya: timeline check — aiming for initial draft assets by 2026-05-18?
[14:40] Olivia: that's our target.
[14:45] Diego: will also include a sample perf spreadsheet and config suggestions for autoscaling policies.
[14:56] Liam: we'll need that perf sheet to size our images for marketplace users.
[15:05] Olivia: any blockers?
[15:09] Sofia: nothing on our end, just need SOC2 pointer.
[15:14] Priya: none.
[15:20] Olivia: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the thread with links to the drafts and a calendar invite for GTM planning.
[15:35] Diego: I'll upload the network requirements doc and the sample manifest to the shared drive after the call.
[15:45] Maya: and I'll add the SAML metadata sample.
[15:55] Olivia: meeting adjourned.

Notes: small transcription artifacts present (speaker labels and some OCR-like typos).
